mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a 0% return under the same FEDFUNDS regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 7% predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces corporate optimism.
regime_hint: high unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive with a p-value < 0.05 when UNRATE > 7% in the preceding month.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising HOUST (industrial production) exceeding 1050 suggests accelerating demand, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when demand momentum is not sustained beyond 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO below 98.5 indicates weakening manufacturing capacity, which is expected to produce a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains below 98.5 for at least 3 consecutive months without a reversal in SPX 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to be positive due to expectations of future inflation.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when CPIAUCSL change > +0.5% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in PAYEMS and UNRATE above their respective 50th percentiles for two months indicate labor market weakness, predicting a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 50th percentile AND UNRATE > 50th percentile for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative when both proxies are above median (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month moving average of GDPC1 above 14,000 indicates robust consumer demand, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the 3-month GDPC1 > 14,000 window.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS falls by more than 10% in a month, it signals supply-side stress and a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced market confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when RSAFS declines by >10% (p > 0.05).
